rule.description: Operator spelling classification (string-keyed tables mapping operator spellings to operator symbols) is carried by self-contained local tables duplicated across several files instead of one shared home, so a change to the operator vocabulary requires the same small edit in every participating file.
rule.definition: A composite literal of a string-keyed map whose literal keys contain two or more operator spellings of the expression grammar is an operator classification table. The rule reports each such table with file, line, and enclosing scope, ignoring _test.go files. Operator classification is SCATTERED when the reported tables span two or more distinct non-test files; tables confined to one file count as one shared home.

checks.description: Detect self-contained string-keyed classification tables that map operator spellings to operator symbols, and report the set of files carrying them.
checks.detected_relation: pipeline stage -> self-contained local operator spelling classification table
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Operator classification is knowledge about the language's grammar as a whole; when each consuming stage owns its own spelling table, any vocabulary change (new spelling, removed operator, reclassification) must be repeated in every participating file.

excluded.what: single-entry inline literals (e.g. the exponent phase's "**", the "&&"/"||"/"," literals configuring individual precedent planners)
excluded.reason: the rule counts tables carrying two or more operator spellings; one-spelling literals do not restate a vocabulary, and this shape predates the injection on the pinned revision.

excluded.what: symbol-keyed dispatch structures (precedence lookup, stage-symbol dispatch, type-check selection, symbol rendering for error messages)
excluded.reason: these are keyed by operator symbol rather than by spelling; they carry no operator spelling classification and are outside the rule.
test code is not a production owner of the classification; the rule ignores _test.go files.

on the pinned clean revision all spelling tables live in one file (the shared registry beside the operator symbol definitions), so the rule reports them but stays within its single-file shared-home bound and the repository passes.
